text: Dispatch, medic one on scene with a 58 year old male, found sitting at the kitchen table clutching his chest.
He's got crushing central chest pain radiating down the left arm, says it started about forty minutes ago while he was mowing the lawn.
First set of vitals: heart rate 96, blood pressure 150 over 92, SpO2 94 percent on room air, respiratory rate 22.
Patient reports no known allergies, no cardiac history that he's aware of.
Twelve lead shows ST elevation in the inferior leads, we're calling this a STEMI, treating as a level one.
Repeat vitals: heart rate 90, blood pressure 142 over 88, SpO2 96 percent, respiratory rate 20.
Correction on the allergy history, patient has a penicillin allergy bracelet on his right wrist.
Gave him another aspirin to be sure, he wasn't certain he swallowed the first one.
We are ten minutes out, ETA to the ED about fourteen twenty six, requesting cath lab activation.
